newsitem.title: ITALY: ATHLETICS-CROSS-COUNTRY GRAND PRIX CIRCUIT PROPOSED.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-CROSS-COUNTRY GRAND PRIX CIRCUIT PROPOSED.

text.p: Leading European cross-country promoters look set to establish their own Grand Prix circuit within the International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) World Cross Challenge series.
"We want to make it like the Golden Four on the track," said Jos Van Roy, promoter of the Brussels Cross Challenge meeting, on Monday.
"It would work within the existing Cross Challenge structure and offer prize money to European runners," he said.
Details are yet to be finalised and presented to the IAAF but Van Roy indicated the circuit would consist of between four and six meetings.
Among those included in the new circuit would be his own event in Brussels; the meeting in Tourcoing, France, and the Cinque Mulini race in San Vittore Olona, Italy.
Van Roy believes the circuit will encourage European distance runners, who are currently lagging behind their African counterparts.
Eight African runners were in the top 10 of the senior men's race at the World Cross-Country championships in Turin on Sunday.
Ironically, one of the two Europeans to prevent an African clean sweep of the leading positions was Mohammed Mourit, a former Moroccan national champion who now runs for Belgium.
European women fared slightly better with four runners in the top 10 of the senior women's race, compared with six Africans.
The IAAF confirmed on Monday their World Cross Challenge series would remain the same next year, with 11 meetings in addition to the World Cross-Country Championships.
There had been suggestions the series was about to shrink further after being reduced by three meetings prior to 1996/97 season.

The only change is that the IAAF have asked the Kenya Amateur Athletic Association to move their event from Nairobi, which is at altitude, to sea-level Mombassa with the intention of encouraging more foreign competitors.
"We cannot expect international runners to have to acclimatise in one or two days," said Alberto Baronet, the IAAF deputy director of competitions.
